correctness.rationale: Direct differentiation gives \(\dot R=2(z-\beta)R\). Because compact support is bounded away from \(R=0\), arbitrary logarithmic-radial antiderivative tests give \(\mathbb E[z\mid R]=\beta\). Arbitrary height antiderivative tests give \(\mathbb E[(1+\rho z)R\mid z]=G(z)\). The pointwise radial identity yields the exact height-variance/activity formula, while conditional orthogonality of \(\dot z\) gives the weighted-load variance decomposition. Zero height variance forces \(z=\beta\), constant radius, and the unique circular orbit when the stated nondegeneracy conditions hold. The exact checker independently verifies the algebra and standard parameter specialization.

value.rationale: The axisymmetric torus is the organizing recurrent object in Langford's classic route from periodic motion toward toroidal and chaotic dynamics. The theorem shows that every off-axis compact recurrent state in that subfamily, regardless of torus amplitude or orbit type, is calibrated to the same exact mean height \(\beta\). More strongly, height is conditionally centered at \(\beta\) at every radius, and its variance is exactly logarithmic radial breathing activity. These identities give parameter-exact diagnostics for numerical tori and periodic states and separate the circular orbit sharply from every radially breathing recurrent state.
